result.summary: The Windows x86_64 build is done and ships as one exe with the PCK embedded. It was checked with pefile and in Wine 9.0 (headless and windowed). New export preset "Windows Desktop": x86_64, S3TC/BPTC, same filters as Linux, no console wrapper for release (export_console_wrapper=1), modify_resources on, product name "Crossing Europe – A Racing Xperience", German description "Crossing Europe – Arcade-Racer quer durch Europa". When the file/product version fields are empty, Godot 4.7.2 fills them from application/config/version (0.4.0 becomes the string 0.4.0.0, numeric version too). So no version injection is needed, and the exe will show 0.5.0.0 after the bump. Company and copyright are empty because the repo names no author or studio. The project's windows_native_icon setting now points to assets/icons/app_icon.ico; Godot packs that file into the PCK automatically. The icon has 7 sizes (16 to 128 px as 32-bit BMP, 256 px as PNG) and is pixel-identical to marketing/steam/icon.ico. Two problems in Godot 4.7.2's exporter: it keeps only 16/32/48/64/128/256 px, and it writes a broken name for the icon group (the name offset points into a directory table, so the group is called ""). The new step tools/windows/set_exe_icon.py fixes both after export. It needs only the Python standard library, rebuilds .rsrc with all 7 frames as group GODOT_ICON, keeps the version info and manifest unchanged, moves .reloc and the pck section back, recalculates the checksum, checks its own output, and gives the same file when run twice. tools/windows/inspect_exe.py checks the exe with pefile. New scripts tools/build_windows.sh and tools/build_release.sh; build_linux.sh is unchanged. Platform audit found one real Windows problem, now fixed in settings.gd: on scaled desktops (125/150/200 %) the window stayed 1280×720 pixels, which looks tiny at 200 %. On Windows only, the window now grows with the scaling (capped to what fits on screen), and the fullscreen-by-default rule uses the scaled height. Linux and Steam Deck behaviour is unchanged; 3 new unit tests. Docs: docs/windows.md (German), one README paragraph, two short ARCHITECTURE.md entries. tools/run_tests.sh: 339 unit tests, 0 failed; session and escape checks OK.

wine_results: CRASH at start of every Godot 4.7.2 Windows template in Wine 9.0, even 'windows_release_x86_64.exe --version': 'Unhandled page fault on read access to 0 at 6FFFFF4B0608'. Relay trace: Godot loads dinput8.dll, patches its import table (GetProcAddress/GetOverlappedResult), then calls VirtualProtect(addr, 8, prot, NULL). Wine 9.0's kernelbase VirtualProtect dereferences old_prot unconditionally (cmp $8,(%rbx)). Real Windows returns FALSE/ERROR_NOACCESS instead. Workaround for all tests: WINEDLLOVERRIDES=dinput8=d. Not a problem of our build.

issues.area: Release archives / license notices (zip layout)
issues.problem: The Windows zip, like the Linux tar.gz, contains only the executable. No Godot Engine MIT license or Godot third-party notices (FreeType, mbedTLS, ENet …) are shipped, no SIL OFL texts for the 4 embedded fonts, and no attribution for the map data. The game has no in-game credits or license screen, and the OFL texts are not in the PCK either. This is pre-existing for Linux, but tools/build_windows.sh:28 repeats it in the new Windows package. MIT and OFL both require the notice to ship with the distributed copy.
issues.evidence: zipinfo -v build/CrossingEurope-windows-x86_64.zip → 'central directory contains 1 entry' (CrossingEurope.exe). tar -tvzf build/CrossingEurope-linux-x86_64.tar.gz → only CrossingEurope.x86_64. Repo-vs-pack mapping (review-binary/repo_vs_pck.txt) → 'MISSING assets/fonts/OFL-BarlowCondensed.txt, OFL-Exo2.txt, OFL-Orbitron.txt, OFL-ShareTechMono.txt'. grep -rniE 'lizenz|license|copyright|Godot Engine|credits|get_license' scripts/ scenes/ → no hits. One option is a small headless script (e.g. tools/print_licenses.gd) that prints Engine.get_license_text(), Engine.get_copyright_info() and Engine.get_license_info(); then append assets/fonts/OFL-*.txt and the Natural Earth / world-atlas (ISC) note. Add the file to both archives: tools/build_windows.sh:28 `zip … CrossingEurope.exe LIZENZEN.txt`, and the tar call in tools/build_release.sh. Mention the file in docs/windows.md and add 'Godot Engine (MIT), godotengine.org/license' to README §Lizenzen.

A stale CrossingEurope.x86_64 could therefore be tarred and checksummed together with a fresh exe. The current build/ artifacts carry 0.4.0.0, although they are meant for v0.5.0.

issues.area: Unsigned exe: Smart App Control / AV not documented
issues.problem: docs/windows.md only covers the SmartScreen 'Weitere Informationen → Trotzdem ausführen' path. On Windows 11 PCs with Smart App Control on, an unsigned exe without reputation is blocked and there is no run-anyway button. New unsigned 420 MB exes are also sometimes flagged by Defender's ML heuristics. Affected users get a hard block and no hint in the docs.
issues.evidence: docs/windows.md:16-21. pe_overview.py shows no DD[4] (security directory), i.e. unsigned. set_exe_icon.py:266-268 deliberately refuses signed input.
issues.fix: Add a short paragraph to docs/windows.md: Smart App Control only allows signed apps; the workaround is to turn it off in Windows-Sicherheit → App- & Browsersteuerung. Before each release, upload the exe to VirusTotal and submit false positives to Microsoft. Long term, sign the exe after set_exe_icon.py (e.g. SignPath Foundation for open source, or Azure Trusted Signing).

Smart App Control (Windows 11) blocks unsigned apps completely when it is on, with no 'Trotzdem ausführen'. Edge and Chrome warn before keeping an uncommon archive that contains an unsigned exe. issues.problem: The exe and the Linux binary are byte-reproducible, but the zip and tar.gz carry build-time mtimes and a gzip timestamp. Every run therefore gives new archive hashes. Re-running the build between upload and publishing SHA256SUMS breaks verification for users, and nobody else can reproduce the published archive hashes.

The exe (fadcbd698cb1…) and the x86_64 (30be8586015b…) are identical. zipinfo shows '26-Nov-01 14:45', tar -tv shows '2026-11-01 14:45'. Code: tools/build_release.sh:15, tools/build_windows.sh:28.

issues.area: tools/build_windows.sh error handling
issues.problem: When pefile is missing, the check of version, icon and subsystem is skipped without any message. A release machine without pefile reports success without the version check. set_exe_icon.py's own verify() covers only the icon and the PCK.

issues.area: Keyboard layouts (key hints)
issues.problem: The driving actions are bound to physical key positions (QWERTY), but the options screen, the tutorial and the README label them with QWERTY letters. QWERTZ (German) matches. On AZERTY the keys are labeled Q/D for steering, Z for gas and S for brake, so French and Belgian players see wrong hints. The arrow keys work on every layout.
issues.evidence: scripts/core/input_setup.gd:52-55 (`e.physical_keycode = code`) with KEY_A/KEY_D/KEY_W/KEY_S at :16-19. Labels: scripts/ui/screens/options_screen.gd:125-127 ('Pfeil links/rechts, A D', 'Pfeil hoch, W', 'Pfeil runter, S'), scripts/race/tutorial_coach.gd:82-83, README.md:79-81.

issues.area: Settings persistence / atomic writes on Windows
issues.problem: settings.json is truncated and rewritten in place, while savegame and leaderboards use JsonFile.save_atomic. A crash or power loss during that write loses the fullscreen setting, the volumes and the player name. Even save_atomic is not atomic on Windows: Godot's rename deletes the target and then calls MoveFileW. A crash in between leaves only <file>.tmp (newest) and .bak, and load_dict ignores .tmp. At most one stage of progress is lost, and the code comment correctly limits its claim to POSIX.
issues.evidence: scripts/core/settings.gd:67-75 (FileAccess.open(PATH, WRITE)); scripts/data/json_file.gd:36-41 (load_dict reads only path and .bak) and :63-75; Godot 4.7.2-stable drivers/windows/dir_access_windows.cpp:338-345 (`remove(new_path)` then `MoveFileW`; copy in …/review-code/godot-src/).
issues.fix: save_settings(): use `JsonFile.save_atomic(PATH, d)`, and load with JsonFile.load_dict so the .bak fallback applies. Optionally, in load_dict, also try `path + TMP_SUFFIX` last when it parses.

issues.area: Release archive contents: licenses
issues.problem: Neither the zip/tar.gz nor the PCK contains license notices: the Godot MIT notice and its third-party list, the SIL OFL texts of the four bundled fonts, and Natural Earth / world-atlas (ISC). There is no in-game credits page either. This already applied to the Linux releases; the Windows zip is a new distribution with the same gap.
issues.evidence: zipinfo CrossingEurope-windows-x86_64.zip → 1 entry (CrossingEurope.exe); tar -tvzf → 1 entry. assets/fonts/OFL-BarlowCondensed.txt, OFL-Exo2.txt, OFL-Orbitron.txt and OFL-ShareTechMono.txt are not matched by include_filter "*.json, *.f32" (export_presets.cfg:10 and :40). grep -i 'license|lizenz|godot engine|Open Font' over scripts/ finds no credits text.

Put it into both archives in build_release.sh and build_windows.sh (zip and tar it next to the binary), or add a 'Lizenzen' page in the options screen.

result.summary:
I checked every review finding and fixed all confirmed medium findings and the cheap low ones, in two commits on top of e3a3b1c: 3ee1799 (fixes) and ce07e56 (docs results). One medium finding was wrong and is rejected with source evidence (see deviations).

**Licences:** New tools/write_licenses.gd writes LIZENZEN.txt (114 KB, deterministic). It contains:
- the Godot MIT licence and the third-party notices of its 102 components with 19 licence texts, all read from the engine itself;
- the 4 OFL font texts;
- the Natural Earth / world-atlas notice (ISC text added as data/map/LICENSE-world-atlas.txt).

The zip and the tar.gz now each contain the program plus LIZENZEN.txt, and SHA256SUMS lists it too.

**Release guards (tools/build_release.sh <Version>):** The script now stops when:
- the version argument is missing or differs from config/version;
- the tree has uncommitted changes (ALLOW_DIRTY=1 allows test builds);
- pefile is missing;
- the build itself changes project files.

It also deletes all old outputs first and checks that the Linux binary exists. It writes build/BUILDINFO.txt (version, commit, commit time, Godot version, checksums). Archives are reproducible: file times are set to the commit time (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH), with `TZ=UTC zip -X`, `tar --sort/--mtime/numeric owner` and `gzip -n`. A second Windows build of the same commit gave identical exe, zip and LIZENZEN.txt; re-packing the tar.gz gave the same hash.

**tools/build_windows.sh:** Prints a warning when pefile is missing (mandatory under REQUIRE_PEFILE=1). The check now also enforces ProductName and FileDescription equal to the game name (read from project.godot) and uses EXPECT_VERSION when set. The zip is reproducible.

**export_presets.cfg:**
- `build/*` is excluded in both presets. I tested this in a scratch project: with the old filter, build/*.json was packed; with the new one it is not.
- FileDescription is now "Crossing Europe – A Racing Xperience", the name Task Manager shows.

**scripts/core/settings.gd:**
- Closing the window (X or Alt+F4) saves the settings, but only if something changed and never in sample mode.
- settings.json is written atomically with JsonFile.save_atomic, keeping a .bak; loading uses load_dict, so a damaged file falls back to the .bak.
- On Windows the window is now fitted into the usable screen area in both directions. It can be smaller than 1280×720, never below half that size. It is centred by its frame using the real decoration offsets, so the title bar is never above the screen. A window that already has the right size and fits is left where it is.
- Linux and Steam Deck behaviour is unchanged.

**Tests and docs:** 3 new unit test methods; 342 tests, 0 failed; integration and escape checks OK. Doc changes:
- docs/windows.md: download protections (browser warnings, SmartScreen, Smart App Control, Defender with false-positive link), a graphics troubleshooting section (force ANGLE through a shortcut, turn it off through override.cfg), a release checklist, SHA256SUMS from v0.5.0, the registry claim corrected, a file-extension hint with the log lines to look for, `settings.json(+.bak)`, the ANGLE skip under Wine, and the new check results.
- README: the platform row, the Steam paragraph and the licence section now mention Windows.
- ARCHITECTURE.md: build tools entry updated.

**Builds:** The final build at ce07e56 passed all checks; the exe check reports OK.

deviations: REJECTED (wine, medium) 'No automatic ANGLE switch without OpenGL 3.3'. The reviewer's evidence comes from a Wine-only code path. Godot 4.7.2 platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:8192 runs the fallback only under `if (fallback && !is_wine && rendering_driver == "opengl3")`, where is_wine is set from ntdll's wine_get_version at line 7816. On Windows, detect_wgl() (platform/windows/wgl_detect_version.cpp, fetched at ed1daf0bf) leaves version=0 when wglCreateContextAttribsARB is missing or the 3.3 core context fails. Line 8223 then switches to ANGLE. The reviewer's guess that Godot assumes 3.3 is wrong, and the docs statement is correct for Windows. Docs were still improved: a 'Fehlerbehebung: Grafik' section, and a Wine note saying Godot skips the ANGLE choice there.

NOT DONE (wine fix 2): the CrossingEurope-Kompatibilitaet.bat launcher in the zip. Godot switches to ANGLE automatically on Windows, so a .bat would only cover the rare case of a broken but present GL 3.3 driver. It would flash a console window and look suspicious to antivirus tools. Instead the docs describe a shortcut with --rendering-driver opengl3_angle and override.cfg with gl_compatibility/fallback_to_angle=false. Reading of override.cfg next to the exe was verified in Wine.

NOT DONE (wine, medium, ANGLE picture): the ANGLE picture cannot be verified without real Windows, and Microsoft's d3dcompiler is external code. force_angle_on_devices keeps Godot's defaults, which are deliberate workarounds for known-bad drivers. Mitigations: a way out for players in the docs, an OpenGL ES 3 check on Linux, and a real-Windows test as release checklist step 6.

NOT CHANGED (binary, low, window/taskbar icon): the only evidence is Wine's own icon scaling. A separate 16–48 px window .ico trades high-DPI quality (Alt+Tab at 200 %) for 100 % quality, and that cannot be judged without real Windows. It is listed under 'Nicht geprüft' in docs/windows.md.

NOT CHANGED (binary, low, optional): the VS_VERSIONINFO language 0x0409 → 0x0407. It is cosmetic and would need a binary patch of the version resource, which set_exe_icon.py deliberately keeps byte for byte. Documented ('Sprache … bei Godot fest Englisch (USA)').
NOT CHANGED (binary, low, user data folder): moving it to %APPDATA%\Crossing Europe is a product decision and would make Windows differ from Linux. Left for the lead (see notes).

DEFERRED (code, low, AZERTY key hints): not Windows-specific, and it needs changes in scripts/ui/screens/options_screen.gd and scripts/race/tutorial_coach.gd, which the UI agent is changing. Arrow keys work on every layout.

PARTLY (code, low, atomic writes): settings now use JsonFile.save_atomic/load_dict. The optional '.tmp fallback' in JsonFile.load_dict is not done. It only helps if a crash hits the microseconds between Godot's DeleteFile and MoveFileW on Windows. save_game.gd and leaderboard_store.gd use their own load loops, so a consistent fix would touch three data-module files. That merge risk is not worth it for this edge case.

SCOPE: the v0.5.0 tag and the public GitHub release were not touched (no push or tag changes allowed). The branch side of the finding is done: version argument, clean-tree check, BUILDINFO and a checklist in docs/windows.md. config/version stays 0.4.0, so the current build/ files are stamped 0.4.0.0.
